Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-6681", "title": "Guide to Good Posture", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Good posture is about more than standing up straight so you can look your best."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is an important part of your long-term health."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Making sure that you hold your body the right way, whether you are moving or still, can prevent pain, injuries, and other health problems."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are two types: Dynamic posture is how you hold yourself when you are moving, like when you are walking, running, or bending over to pick up something."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Static posture is how you hold yourself when you are not moving, like when you are sitting, standing, or sleeping."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It is important to make sure that you have good dynamic and static posture."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The key to good posture is the position of your spine."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your spine has three natural curves - at your neck, mid back, and low back."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Correct posture should maintain these curves, but not increase them."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Your head should be above your shoulders, and the top of your shoulder should be over the hips."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Poor posture can be bad for your health."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Slouching or slumping over can: Misalign your musculoskeletal system Wear away at your spine, making it more fragile and prone to injury Cause neck, shoulder, and back pain Decrease your flexibility Affect how well your joints move Affect your balance and increase your risk of falling Make it harder to digest your food Make it harder to breathe How can I improve my posture in general?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Be mindful of your posture during everyday activities, like watching television, washing dishes, or walking Stay active."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Any kind of exercise may help improve your posture, but certain types of exercises can be especially helpful."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "They include yoga, tai chi, and other classes that focus on body awareness."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It is also a good idea to do exercises that strengthen your core (muscles around your back, abdomen, and pelvis)."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Extra weight can weaken your abdominal muscles, cause problems for your pelvis and spine, and contribute to low back pain."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "High heels, for example, can throw off your balance and force you to walk differently."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "This puts more stress on your muscles and harms your posture."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Make sure work surfaces are at a comfortable height for you, whether you're sitting in front of a computer, making dinner, or eating a meal."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "How can I improve my posture when sitting?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Many Americans spend a lot of their time sitting - either at work, at school, or at home."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "It is important to sit properly, and to take frequent breaks: Switch sitting positions often Take brief walks around your office or home Gently stretch your muscles every so often to help relieve muscle tension Don't cross your legs; keep your feet on the floor, with your ankles in front of your knees Make sure that your feet touch the floor, or if that's not possible, use a footrest Relax your shoulders; they should not be rounded or pulled backwards Keep your elbows in close to your body."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "They should be bent between 90 and 120 degrees."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Make sure that your back is fully supported."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Use a back pillow or other back support if your chair does not have a backrest that can support your lower back's curve."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Make sure that your thighs and hips are supported."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "You should have a well-padded seat, and your thighs and hips should be parallel to the floor."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "How can I improve my posture when standing?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Stand up straight and tall Keep your shoulders back Pull your stomach in Put your weight mostly on the balls of your feet Keep your head level Let your arms hang down naturally at your sides Keep your feet about shoulder-width apart With practice, you can improve your posture; you will look and feel better."}]}, {"id": "MLP-6621", "title": "Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) Treatment", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "An alcohol use disorder (AUD) is drinking that causes distress and harm."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is a medical condition in which you: Drink alcohol compulsively Can't control how much you drink Feel anxious, irritable, and/or stressed when you are not drinking An AUD can range from mild to severe, depending on the symptoms."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Severe AUD is sometimes called alcoholism or alcohol dependence."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "What are the treatments for alcohol use disorder?"}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Most people with an alcohol use disorder can benefit from some form of treatment."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Medical treatments include medicines and behavioral therapies."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "For many people, using both types gives them the best results."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "People who are getting treatment for AUD may also find it helpful to go to a support group such as Alcoholics Anonymous (AA)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "If you have an AUD and a mental illness, it is important to get treatment for both."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Some people may need intensive treatment for AUD."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They may go to a residential treatment center for rehabilitation (rehab)."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It usually includes several different kinds of behavioral therapies."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It may also include medicines for detox (medical treatment for alcohol withdrawal) and/or for treating the AUD."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Which medicines can treat alcohol use disorder?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Three medicines are approved to treat AUD: Disulfiram causes unpleasant symptoms such as nausea and skin flushing whenever you drink alcohol."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Knowing that drinking will cause these unpleasant effects may help you stay away from alcohol."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Naltrexone blocks the receptors in your brain that make you feel good when you drink alcohol."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It can also reduce your craving for alcohol."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "This can help you cut back on your drinking."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Acamprosate helps you avoid alcohol after you have quit drinking."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "It works on multiple brain systems to reduce your cravings, especially just after you have quit drinking."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Your health care provider can help you figure out if one of these medicines is right for you."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "They are not addictive, so you don't have to worry about trading one addiction for another."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "They are not a cure, but they can help you manage AUD."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "This is just like taking medicines to manage a chronic disease such as asthma or diabetes."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Which behavioral therapies can treat alcohol use disorder?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Another name for behavioral therapies for AUD is alcohol counseling."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "It involves working with a health care professional to identify and help change the behaviors that lead to your heavy drinking.: Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) helps you identify the feelings and situations that can lead to heavy drinking."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "It teaches you coping skills, including how to manage stress and how to change the thoughts that cause you to want to drink."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "You may get CBT one-on-one with a therapist or in small groups."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Motivational enhancement therapy helps you build and strengthen the motivation to change your drinking behavior."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "It includes about four sessions over a short period of time."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The therapy starts with identifying the pros and cons of seeking treatment."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Then you and your therapist work on forming a plan for making changes in your drinking."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "The next sessions focus on building up your confidence and developing the skills you need to be able to stick to the plan."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Marital and family counseling includes spouses and other family members."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "It can help to repair and improve your family relationships."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Studies show that strong family support through family therapy may help you to stay away from drinking."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Brief interventions are short, one-on-one or small-group counseling sessions."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "The counselor gives you information about your drinking pattern and potential risks."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "The counselor works with you to set goals and provide ideas that may help you make a change."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Is treatment for alcohol use disorder effective?"}, {"id": "S042", "text": "For most people, treatment for an AUD is helpful."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "But overcoming an alcohol use disorder is an ongoing process, and you may relapse (start drinking again)."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "You should look at relapse as a temporary setback, and keep trying."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Many people repeatedly try to cut back or quit drinking, have a setback, then try to quit again."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Having a relapse does not mean that you cannot recover."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "If you do relapse, it is important to return to treatment right away, so you can learn more about your relapse triggers and improve your coping skills."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "This may help you be more successful the next time."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "NIH: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1532", "title": "Sciatica", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Sciatica is a symptom of a problem with the sciatic nerve, the largest nerve in the body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It controls muscles in the back of your knee and lower leg and provides feeling to the back of your thigh, part of your lower leg, and the sole of your foot."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "When you have sciatica, you have pain, weakness, numbness, or tingling."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It can start in the lower back and extend down your leg to your calf, foot, or even your toes."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It's usually on only one side of your body."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Causes of sciatica include: A ruptured intervertebral disk Narrowing of the spinal canal that puts pressure on the nerve, called spinal stenosis An injury such as a pelvic fracture."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Sometimes sciatica goes away on its own."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Treatment, if needed, depends on the cause of the problem."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It may include exercises, medicines, and surgery."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3585", "title": "Benign Tumors", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Tumors are abnormal growths in your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They cannot spread or invade other parts of your body."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Even so, they can be dangerous if they press on vital organs, such as your brain."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Normally, cells grow and divide to form new cells as your body needs them."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "When cells grow old, they die, and new cells take their place."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "New cells form when your body does not need them, and old cells do not die when they should."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "These extra cells can divide without stopping and may form a tumor."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3192", "title": "Cancer Alternative Therapies", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What are complementary and alternative therapies for cancer care?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You have many choices to make about your cancer treatment."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "One choice you might consider is using complementary and alternative medicine (CAM)."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "CAM is the term for medical products and therapies that are not part of standard medical care."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "CAM for cancer treatment involves caring for your mind, body, and spirit."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some methods focus on your breathing or body movements to help you relax."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Other CAM therapies may use special foods, supplements , or diets."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Examples of CAM therapies include acupuncture , chiropractic , and herbal medicines ."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "CAM claims can sound promising, but often, researchers don't know how safe some are or how well they work."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Studies are ongoing to find out the safety and usefulness of many of these methods."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "How are complementary and alternative therapies used for cancer care?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If you're thinking about using CAM along with your standard care, it's called integrative medicine."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Some methods, such as acupuncture, might help with nausea , pain, and other side effects of cancer treatment."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "A few reasons that people with cancer may use CAM include to: Help cope with the side effects of cancer treatments Ease worries about cancer treatment and related stress Feel that they are doing something more to help their care CAM treatments don't work for everyone."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Some products might interact with your other medicines."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Talk to your health care provider about all the different types of treatment you use."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Your provider can help you make sure that everything you're using for your cancer care works well together."}]}]
